theme: The genealogy; the birth; the Magi, new Israel begins
readingInstruction: Read Matthew 1:1-2:23. The New Testament opens with a list of names. Read it as the final page of the Old Testament’s story, then follow the child from Bethlehem to Egypt and back to Nazareth.
settingTheScene: After four hundred years of prophetic silence, the first words of the New Testament are “The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.” Matthew was a tax collector who became one of the Twelve, and he writes mainly for Jewish readers. His aim is to show that Jesus is the one the whole Old Testament was waiting for. He quotes or echoes Israel’s Scriptures more than any other Gospel writer, and he says again and again that something happened “to fulfill what the Lord had spoken by the prophet.”
observation: “The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham” (1:1).
“And Judah the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar” (1:3).
“And Salmon the father of Boaz by Rahab, and Boaz the father of Obed by Ruth” (1:5).
“You shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins” (1:21).
“And they shall call his name Immanuel (which means, God with us)” (1:23).
“Where is he who has been born king of the Jews? For we saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him” (2:2).
“And you, O Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah” (2:6).
“Out of Egypt I called my son” (2:15).
interpretation:
Matthew’s genealogy is a short history of the covenants. It begins with Abraham, to whom God promised a blessing for all nations, and moves to David, to whom God promised a throne that would never end. It ends at the exile and then with Jesus. Matthew arranges it in three sets of fourteen, a pattern that is itself a quiet claim: David’s line, broken in Babylon, has now arrived at its Messiah.

Notice who is in the list. Four women are named, which was unusual in a genealogy: Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and the wife of Uriah. Several were outsiders and some were involved in scandal. Matthew is telling us at the outset that the Messiah comes through the real, messy story of sinners and foreigners, and that grace has been at work in his family tree all along.

The birth story is told from Joseph’s side. He is a righteous man who plans to quietly end the engagement, and God steps in. The name Jesus means “the LORD saves,” and the angel gives its meaning: he will save his people from their sins. That is a bigger rescue than overthrowing Rome. Then Isaiah’s promise is quoted: Immanuel, God with us. The book will end with Jesus saying, “I am with you always,” so the whole Gospel is framed by that promise.

In chapter 2, foreign astrologers come to worship the new king while the king in Jerusalem is troubled and the religious experts know where he will be born but do not go. Herod tries to kill the child. Jesus is taken to Egypt and brought back, and Matthew quotes Hosea: “Out of Egypt I called my son.” Hosea was speaking about Israel in the exodus. Matthew sees Jesus as the true Israel, who relives the nation’s story and does what it failed to do.
connection: Genesis 12:3 promised that all families of the earth would be blessed through Abraham, and the Magi are the first fruits of that. 2 Samuel 7:12-13 is the promise of David’s throne. Isaiah 7:14 is the Immanuel passage you read in Unit 11. Micah 5:2 names Bethlehem. Romans 5:20 says that where sin increased, grace abounded all the more. Galatians 4:4-5 says that in the fullness of time God sent his Son to redeem those under the law.
application:
Read the genealogy aloud, slowly, and thank God for the sinners and outsiders in it. Then thank him that your own story is not too messy for his grace.

Ask what it would mean to treat Jesus as “God with us” in your ordinary Tuesday.

Notice the difference between the Magi and the scribes: one group traveled far to worship, and the other knew the Bible and stayed home. Which are you more like this week?
prayerPrompts: Thank God for keeping every promise to Abraham and David in Jesus.
Tell him what it means that Jesus came to save his people from their sins.
Ask him to teach you to worship as the Magi did.
